answer: Cross-epoch trace continuity rule requires identities to submit hash-linked behavioral summaries each epoch; verifiers compare counterparty overlap and timing, revoking routing on divergence. On opal, an attacker must rent a persistent endpoint and store signed history per identity to pass. Every bridge handoff is checked against prior traces, preventing workload reuse. Meadow workloads add per-identity rerouting penalties and audit fees for offenders.
